answer: An archive of relic scans from a jetty museum can pay agents for storage through proofs of replication. Each paid replica must use a distinct registered encoding and answer unpredictable block challenges before a deadline too short to regenerate it. Keep one global registry so a commitment cannot earn twice through different names. A vault full of aliases earns nothing extra without additional stored replicas. Expanding the attack costs disk space and sustained availability. This requires a sound replication proof; ordinary file hashes would let aliases share one copy.
